about.metaDescription: About Boundary Notes, and the work on real-time speech, system architecture and engineering practice recorded here.
about.headline:
Looking for clear boundaries

inside complex systems.
about.intro: I am yty. This is where I write about real-time speech systems, software architecture and engineering practice — more concerned with why a decision holds than with listing tools and conclusions.
about.body1: Most technical writing tells you how to do something, and rarely says why this particular boundary, what it protects, or under what conditions it should be revisited.
about.body1Strong: Boundary Notes is an attempt at that second half.
about.body2: Most of what I build sits close to hard constraints: real-time speech on CPU alone, observable event pipelines, and a balance between latency and false triggers reached through policy rather than one magic threshold. Writing the trade-offs down is how I avoid forgetting why they were made.
about.focus1Description: AEC, noise suppression, VAD, streaming ASR, barge-in and response cancellation — getting a real-time pipeline to hold up under real constraints.
about.focus2Description: Session state machines, event pipelines, boundaries and where responsibility sits. First say where the data went, then talk about scaling.
about.focus3Description: Rendering pipelines, inference optimisation, security boundaries and observability — and the details that only bite once something ships.
about.work1Description: A CPU-only barge-in system for conversational avatars, coordinating the acoustic chain, timing boundaries and business-level cancellation around one session state machine.
about.work2Description: A self-built Next.js blog: server-rendered Markdown, inline Mermaid SVG, revision diffs and a media library — an engineering sample that keeps evolving.
